prompt: The line graph shows how many people travelled to work by car, bus and bicycle in a European city between 2000 and 2020. Describe the most important trends and differences, using figures from the graph to support your description. Write at least 150 words.

visual.title: Commuters by mode of transport, 2000–2020
facts: Car fell from 420 thousand in 2000 to 300 thousand in 2020 (-28.6%).
Car was highest in 2005 (450 thousand) and lowest in 2020 (300 thousand).
Bus rose from 210 thousand in 2000 to 330 thousand in 2020 (+57.1%).
Bus was highest in 2020 (330 thousand) and lowest in 2000 (210 thousand).
Bicycle stayed about the same from 40 thousand in 2000 to 41 thousand in 2020 (+2.5%).
Bicycle was highest in 2005 (42 thousand) and lowest in 2000 (40 thousand).
In 2000 the highest was Car; in 2020 it was Bus.
The largest increase was in Bus (+120 thousand).
The largest decrease was in Car (−120 thousand).
Car and Bus changed places between 2015 and 2020.

text:
The line graph illustrates how many commuters in a European city used cars, buses and bicycles to travel to work at five-year intervals between 2000 and 2020. Figures are given in thousands.

Cars were the dominant choice at the start of the period, with 420 thousand commuters in 2000. This figure climbed to a peak of 450 thousand in 2005 before dropping to 430 thousand in 2010. The decline then accelerated, with the number falling to 380 thousand in 2015 and to 300 thousand in 2020, a decrease of 120 thousand compared with the starting point.

Bus use followed the opposite course. Starting at 210 thousand, it grew consistently in every period, reaching 260 thousand in 2010 and 330 thousand in 2020, an increase of 120 thousand. The two lines crossed between 2015, when buses stood at 300 thousand and cars at 380 thousand, and 2020. Cycling, by contrast, fluctuated only between 40 and 42 thousand.
